title: Borromean Criticality in Two Dimensions
authors: Alexandru Golic, Igor Timoshuk, Albert Samoilenka, Egor Babaev, Boris Svistunov
abstract: The characteristic feature of counterflow superfluids consisting of $N\geq 3$ components -- the so-called Borromean supercounterfluids (BSCF) -- is the presence of $N$ distinct elementary topological excitations (vortices) despite having only $N-1$ independent Goldstone modes. We show that this remarkable property clearly manifests itself at the Berezinskii-Kosterlitz-Thouless-type transition from the BSCF to the normal state, under the conditions of slight to moderate deviations from the case of exact intercomponent symmetry. More generally, our analysis also applies to any multicomponent superfluid with intercomponent drag fine-tuned to the value when certain composite vortices compete energetically with elementary ones.
summary: This work analyzes the critical phase transition in Borromean Supercounterfluids (BSCF) in 2D, a system characterized by more topological excitations than Goldstone modes. Using Renormalization Group theory, the authors derive scaling laws that predict a BKT-type transition, providing quantitative predictions for superfluid stiffnesses near the critical point.
main_problem: The paper investigates the Berezinskii-Kosterlitz-Thouless (BKT)-type phase transition in Borromean Supercounterfluids (BSCF) in two dimensions, especially when symmetry is slightly broken.
main_result: The critical behavior is predicted to be BKT-type, and the analysis yields explicit scaling laws for superfluid stiffnesses and phase boundaries, showing how topological excitations govern the transition.
method: The primary method involves developing and solving Renormalization Group (RG) equations for the system's effective action, analyzing flow equations in different proximity regimes to critical points.
model_or_system: The system is a counterflow superfluid (SCF) with $N \ge 3$ components, modeled using the J-current model or a two-component representation of a BSCF. The key feature is the existence of $N$ elementary topological excitations despite $N-1$ Goldstone modes.
key_observables: Superfluid stiffnesses ($\Lambda_s, \Lambda_d$), vortex fugacities ($g_s, g_d$), and correlation lengths ($\lambda_c$).
important_parameters: The asymmetry parameter ($\Gamma$ or $\xi$), the golden ratio constant ($\varphi$), and the critical coupling constants ($\xi^{(c)}_s, \xi^{(c)}_d$).
main_assumptions: The analysis relies on linearizing the RG equations near the symmetric point and making approximations regarding the smallness of asymmetry parameters.
figures_summary: Figures illustrate scaling functions for superfluid stiffnesses, the phase diagram showing boundaries dependent on the golden ratio, and the flow of correlation lengths with system size.
paper_structure: The paper progresses by establishing the RG framework for the multicomponent superfluid, analyzing the symmetric limit, then introducing asymmetry via coupled RG equations, and finally deriving explicit scaling solutions for different proximity regimes to the critical point.
why_interesting: The study provides a deep theoretical understanding of topological phase transitions in multicomponent superfluids, connecting concepts like Goldstone modes, vortex physics, and critical exponents using advanced RG techniques.
